title: Stochastic Voronoi Ensembles for Anomaly Detection
Stochastic Voronoi Ensembles for Anomaly Detection
summary: Anomaly detection methods struggle with data exhibiting varying local densities, where distance-based methods miss local anomalies and density-based methods require careful parameter selection and incur quadratic time complexity. SVEAD constructs an ensemble of random Voronoi diagrams by sampling anchors, scores points by normalized cell-relative distance weighted by local scale, and averages scores across partitions. Across 45 ADBench datasets it achieves the highest average AUC-ROC (0.8538) and AUC-PR (0.5000) among 12 baselines, including 0.9339 AUC-ROC on cardio, while maintaining linear time and constant space complexity.

approach: Route is paper_only with no author repository on disk (only an uncloned anonymous.4open.science link), so SVEAD is reimplemented from the paper: for each of t=100 partitions, sample m anchors uniformly without replacement, assign every point to its nearest anchor in standardized feature space (implicit Voronoi, no cell boundaries), score each point as (delta/delta_max) * delta_mean inside its cell, skip singleton cells, and average the per-partition scores. The match target is C1: AUC-ROC 0.9339 on ADBench cardio (1831 samples, 21 features, 176 anomalies); the dataset is fetched at runtime through a validated fallback chain (ADBench GitHub raw -> OpenML cardiotocography -> UCI Cardiotocography), all of which reduce to exactly the same 1831x21 table with 176 positives, and a hard validation gate asserts that shape before any scoring. The m hyperparameter is grid-searched over {2,4,...,256} with 5 seeded repeats per value and t=100, matching the paper's protocol (R7, R8); we report both the label-tuned best m and the full m-curve so the +/-0.0189 tolerance band is interpretable, plus AUC-PR (C2) for free from the same runs. C3/C4 (45 datasets) and C5/C6 (GPU 500k-instance scalability) are explicitly out of scope on this CPU-only machine and are flagged as 'not reproduced' in the output.
steps: Install/verify deps: `pip install numpy scipy pandas scikit-learn matplotlib requests tqdm openpyxl xlrd`; confirm sklearn.datasets.fetch_openml and sklearn.metrics imports succeed.

Write svead/data.py with a priority loader and an on-disk cache at data/cardio.npz: (1) local cache; (2) ADBench GitHub — GET https://api.github.com/repos/Minqi824/ADBench/git/trees/main?recursive=1, find any path containing 'cardio' ending in .csv/.npz/.arff, download via raw.githubusercontent.com; (3) sklearn.datasets.fetch_openml(data_id=1466) or name='cardiotocography' — take the 21 feature columns, keep rows with NSP in {1,3}, label = (NSP == 3); (4) UCI fallback https://archive.ics.uci.edu/static/public/193/cardiotocography.zip -> CTG.xls, same 21-feature/NSP filter.

Validate the loaded table in svead/data.py: assert X.shape == (1831, 21), y.sum() == 176, mean(y) ~= 0.0961, no NaN/inf (assumption A6); if any assertion fails on a fallback source, log the mismatch into the provenance dict and continue, because the source is then not guaranteed to be the ADBench cardio table.

Write svead/svead_core.py: sample_anchors(X, m, rng) -> unique row indices (R1); assign_cells(X, A, chunk_rows) -> (cell_ids, delta) using chunked Euclidean distance and argmin with lowest-index tie-break (R2, R11); cell_stats -> per-cell delta_max and delta_mean computed for all points before any scoring (R4); score_partition -> s = (delta / delta_max) * delta_mean with NaN for singleton cells and a delta_max == 0 guard (R3, R5); svead_score(X, m, t, seed) -> nanmean over t partitions, 0 if all NaN, plus diagnostics (cell-size histogram, skipped fraction, per-partition seconds) (R6, R12).

Write svead/metrics.py: roc_auc_score wrapper, average_precision_score (primary AUC-PR), trapezoidal precision_recall_curve AUC (secondary), and summarize(list) -> mean/std/min/max; all functions take scores first and labels second so labels are consumed only post-prediction (R9, R10).

Run the smoke test: `python experiments/smoke_test.py`. Part A: synthetic 300x6 with 10% Gaussian outliers, m=4, t=3 -> assert finite non-negative scores, shape (300,), AUC-ROC > 0.8. Part B: real cardio, m=8, t=5 -> assert score shape (1831,), deterministic repeat for the same seed, total runtime < 60 s.

Run the pre-full-run intermediate checks below (dataset signature, standardization stats, anchor uniqueness, cell-size/skip diagnostics, a kNN-distance and IsolationForest sanity baseline, single-run timing extrapolation).

Write experiments/run_cardio.py: outer loop over m in the 8-value grid, inner loop over the 5 seeds, each run calling svead_score on the standardized matrix with t=100, recording AUC-ROC, AUC-PR (both variants), wall time, skipped-point fraction and cell statistics; append rows to results/per_m_table.csv and dump raw per-run records to results/raw_cardio.json.

Launch the full suite: `python experiments/run_cardio.py`; after the first two m values finish, check that the extrapolated total stays inside the budget (expected total is only a few minutes because the per-run cost is ~0.1-3 s at these sizes) and only then let it complete.

Select best m = argmax of mean AUC-ROC across the 5 seeds; compute mean/std for AUC-ROC and AUC-PR at that m, and also record the fixed-m=128 (A3 fallback) result and the full m-curve for sensitivity.

Write reproduce.py: load data from cache, reuse or regenerate results/raw_cardio.json, run selection, then write results/metrics.json with (a) C1 value vs 0.9339 with the 0.0189 band and PASS/FAIL verdict, (b) C2 value vs 0.5356, (c) per-m table and per-repeat spreads, (d) dataset provenance and validation flags, (e) timing, (f) the assumption ledger entries applied, (g) an explicit not_reproduced block for C3, C4, C5 and C6 (45-dataset average and GPU/500k scalability are out of scope on CPU).

Run the final entrypoint `python reproduce.py` and read results/metrics.json; report the reproduced C1 with its spread, label the overall verdict partially_reproduced, and never present C3-C6 as reproduced.
smoke_test: `python experiments/smoke_test.py` — synthesizes 300x6 data with 10% outliers at m=4, t=3 and asserts finite non-negative scores, shape (300,), AUC-ROC > 0.8; then scores the full 1831x21 cardio table at m=8, t=5, asserting shape (1831,), reproducible scores for a repeated seed, and under 60 s wall clock. This exercises download -> standardize -> anchor sampling -> nearest-anchor assignment -> cell stats -> scoring -> averaging -> AUC end to end on a few seconds of compute.
intermediate_checks: Dataset signature: X.shape == (1831, 21), y.sum() == 176, anomaly rate 0.0961, zero NaN/inf, and the 21 UCI/ADBench feature names present — abort or flag loudly if a fallback source yields different counts (e.g. 2126 rows means the suspect class was not filtered).
Standardization: after StandardScaler, per-column mean ~ 0 (|mean| < 1e-9) and std ~ 1 for all 21 columns; confirm the scaler is fit with no label access.
Anchor sampling: for every m in the grid and every seed, sampled anchor indices are distinct and len == m (requirement R1), verified on 20 random (m, seed) pairs.

Cell diagnostics: for m=256 on n=1831, singleton cells must be essentially zero and skipped-point fraction < 0.5%; log non-empty cell count, max/mean cell size, and skipped fraction for every (m, seed).

Score sanity: all scores finite and >= 0; distribution roughly right-skewed with a handful of large scores matching injected/synthetic outliers; Spearman correlation with a trivial 1-NN mean-distance baseline is clearly positive.

Sanity baselines on cardio: sklearn IsolationForest(n_estimators=100, random_state=1) and a global kNN mean-distance score; both should land roughly in 0.65-0.85 AUC-ROC — if SVEAD cannot beat them, the reimplementation is wrong, not the paper.
No-cell-means-0 check: with the chosen cell_stats_scope (anchor included at distance 0), delta_mean must still be > 0 for every non-singleton cell; assert this before the full run.

Timing probe: time one full run at m=256, t=100 -> extrapolate the whole 40-run grid; if the extrapolation exceeds ~25 minutes, drop to 3 repeats and/or m in {8,16,32,64,128} (documented as a reduced protocol).
Determinism: two back-to-back runs with identical (m, seed) produce bitwise-identical score vectors.
budget_plan: Total ~90 min on CPU. Setup and data acquisition 15 min (pip installs, the ADBench/OpenML/UCI fallback chain, cache write, dataset-signature validation). Implementation of svead/data.py, svead/svead_core.py and svead/metrics.py 20 min. Smoke test and intermediate checks 10 min (including the IsolationForest/kNN sanity baselines and the timing probe). Full cardio grid 25 min reserved though expected ~5-10 min (8 m values x 5 seeds x t=100 on a 1831x21 matrix; each run is only a few seconds, so sum over m of m makes the whole grid roughly 2x the cost of a single m=256 run per seed). Final reproduce.py + metrics.json writing and interpretation 10 min. Contingency: if a run ever exceeds the projection, first cut repeats from 5 to 3, then narrow the m grid to four values, always recording the reduced protocol in results/metrics.json. C3/C4 (45 datasets) and C5/C6 (500k-instance CPU/GPU timing) are deliberately not scheduled.

import numpy as np
from typing import Tuple, Dict, Any


def sample_anchors(n: int, m: int, rng: np.random.Generator) -> np.ndarray:
    """Sample m unique anchor indices uniformly without replacement."""
    return rng.choice(n, size=m, replace=False)


def assign_cells(
    X: np.ndarray,
    anchors: np.ndarray,
    chunk_rows: int = 4096,
) -> Tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray]:
    """Assign each row of X to its nearest anchor (Euclidean distance).
    Returns (cell_ids, distances) where cell_ids in [0, m) and distances are ||x - a*||.
    Tie-breaking: lowest anchor index (numpy argmin behavior).
    """
    n, d = X.shape
    m = anchors.shape[0]
    cell_ids = np.empty(n, dtype=np.int64)
    distances = np.empty(n, dtype=np.float64)
    for start in range(0, n, chunk_rows):
        end = min(start + chunk_rows, n)
        block = X[start:end]  # (b, d)
        # Compute squared Euclidean distances to all anchors: (b, m)
        # ||x - a||^2 = ||x||^2 + ||a||^2 - 2 x·a^T
        x_norm = np.sum(block ** 2, axis=1, keepdims=True)  # (b, 1)
        a_norm = np.sum(anchors ** 2, axis=1, keepdims=True).T  # (1, m)
        cross = block @ anchors.T  # (b, m)
        dists_sq = x_norm + a_norm - 2.0 * cross
        # Clamp to avoid negative zeros
        dists_sq = np.maximum(dists_sq, 0.0)
        dists = np.sqrt(dists_sq)
        j = np.argmin(dists, axis=1)  # lowest index on ties
        cell_ids[start:end] = j
        # Advanced indexing to get distances
        distances[start:end] = dists[np.arange(end - start), j]
    return cell_ids, distances


def cell_stats(
    X: np.ndarray,
    anchors: np.ndarray,
    cell_ids: np.ndarray,
    distances: np.ndarray,
) -> Tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray]:
    """Compute per-cell delta_max and delta_mean.
    The anchor itself is included in its cell (distance 0).
    """
    m = anchors.shape[0]
    delta_max = np.empty(m, dtype=np.float64)
    delta_mean = np.empty(m, dtype=np.float64)
    for j in range(m):
        mask = cell_ids == j
        if not np.any(mask):
            # Empty cell: degenerate, set max=0, mean=0
            delta_max[j] = 0.0
            delta_mean[j] = 0.0
        else:
            cell_dists = distances[mask]
            delta_max[j] = cell_dists.max()
            delta_mean[j] = cell_dists.mean()
    return delta_max, delta_mean


def score_partition(
    X: np.ndarray,
    anchors: np.ndarray,
    cell_ids: np.ndarray,
    distances: np.ndarray,
    delta_max: np.ndarray,
    delta_mean: np.ndarray,
) -> np.ndarray:
    """Score points in one partition.
    Returns array of shape (n,) with NaN for skipped singleton cells.
    """
    n = X.shape[0]
    scores = np.empty(n, dtype=np.float64)
    # Cell sizes
    cell_sizes = np.bincount(cell_ids, minlength=anchors.shape[0])
    # Delta max for each point's cell
    point_delta_max = delta_max[cell_ids]
    point_delta_mean = delta_mean[cell_ids]
    # Singleton mask
    singleton = cell_sizes[cell_ids] == 1
    # Delta max zero guard
    zero_max = point_delta_max == 0.0
    # Compute raw score
    with np.errstate(divide="ignore", invalid="ignore"):
        ratio = np.where(zero_max, 0.0, distances / point_delta_max)
        scores = ratio * point_delta_mean
    # Skip singleton cells
    scores = np.where(singleton, np.nan, scores)
    return scores


def svead_score(
    X: np.ndarray,
    m: int,
    t: int,
    seed: int,
    chunk_rows: int = 4096,
) -> Tuple[np.ndarray, Dict[str, Any]]:
    """Run SVEAD and return final anomaly scores plus diagnostics."""
    n, d = X.shape
    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed + 1000 * m)
    partition_scores = np.empty((t, n), dtype=np.float64)
    timings = []
    cell_sizes_all = []
    skipped_counts = []

    for k in range(t):
        anchors = sample_anchors(n, m, rng)
        A = X[anchors]
        t0 = __import__("time").perf_counter()
        cell_ids, distances = assign_cells(X, A, chunk_rows=chunk_rows)
        delta_max, delta_mean = cell_stats(X, A, cell_ids, distances)
        s = score_partition(X, A, cell_ids, distances, delta_max, delta_mean)
        partition_scores[k] = s
        t1 = __import__("time").perf_counter()
        timings.append(t1 - t0)
        sizes = np.bincount(cell_ids, minlength=m)
        cell_sizes_all.append(sizes)
        skipped_counts.append(int(np.isnan(s).sum()))

    # Final score: nanmean over partitions; if all NaN -> 0
    with np.errstate(all="ignore"):
        final = np.nanmean(partition_scores, axis=0)
    final = np.where(np.isnan(final), 0.0, final)

    diagnostics = {
        "timings": timings,
        "total_time": float(np.sum(timings)),
        "cell_sizes": cell_sizes_all,
        "skipped_counts": skipped_counts,
        "skipped_fraction": float(np.mean(skipped_counts) / n),
        "m": m,
        "t": t,
        "seed": seed,
        "n": n,
        "d": d,
    }
    return final, diagnostics

    assert scores.shape == (n,), f"Bad shape {scores.shape}"
    assert np.isfinite(scores).all(), "Scores not finite"
    assert (scores >= 0).all(), "Scores negative"

    print(f"SMOKE synthetic AUC-ROC={auc:.4f}")

import os
import sys
import json
import time
import csv
import numpy as np

sys.path.insert(0, os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))))

from svead.data import load_cardio
from svead.svead_core import svead_score
from svead.metrics import evaluate_scores

M_GRID = [2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64, 128, 256]
SEEDS = [1, 2, 3, 4, 5]
T = 100
RESULTS_DIR = "results"
RAW_PATH = os.path.join(RESULTS_DIR, "raw_cardio.json")
TABLE_PATH = os.path.join(RESULTS_DIR, "per_m_table.csv")


def main():
    os.makedirs(RESULTS_DIR, exist_ok=True)
    X, y, prov = load_cardio()
    print(f"Loaded cardio: X{X.shape}, y{np.bincount(y)}")

    records = []
    for m in M_GRID:
        for seed in SEEDS:
            print(f"Running m={m}, seed={seed} ...")
            t0 = time.perf_counter()
            scores, diag = svead_score(X, m=m, t=T, seed=seed)
            dt = time.perf_counter() - t0
            metrics = evaluate_scores(scores, y)
            rec = {
                "m": m,
                "seed": seed,
                "t": T,
                "auc_roc": metrics["auc_roc"],
                "auc_pr_primary": metrics["auc_pr_primary"],
                "auc_pr_trapezoidal": metrics["auc_pr_trapezoidal"],
                "wall_time_s": round(dt, 4),
                "skipped_fraction": round(diag["skipped_fraction"], 6),
                "skipped_counts": diag["skipped_counts"],
                "cell_sizes": [c.tolist() for c in diag["cell_sizes"]],
                "timings": [round(t, 4) for t in diag["timings"]],
            }
            records.append(rec)
            print(f"  -> AUC-ROC={metrics['auc_roc']:.4f} AUC-PR={metrics['auc_pr_primary']:.4f} time={dt:.2f}s")

    with open(RAW_PATH, "w") as f:
        json.dump({
            "records": records,
            "provenance": prov,
            "config": {"m_grid": M_GRID, "seeds": SEEDS, "t": T},
        }, f, indent=2)

    # Write per-m summary table
    with open(TABLE_PATH, "w", newline="") as f:
        writer = csv.writer(f)
        writer.writerow(["m", "mean_auc_roc", "std_auc_roc", "mean_auc_pr", "std_auc_pr", "mean_time_s"])
        for m in M_GRID:
            rows = [r for r in records if r["m"] == m]
            aurocs = [r["auc_roc"] for r in rows]
            auprs = [r["auc_pr_primary"] for r in rows]
            times = [r["wall_time_s"] for r in rows]
            writer.writerow([
                m,
                round(float(np.mean(aurocs)), 6),
                round(float(np.std(aurocs, ddof=1)), 6),
                round(float(np.mean(auprs)), 6),
                round(float(np.std(auprs, ddof=1)), 6),
                round(float(np.mean(times)), 4),
            ])
    print(f"Wrote {RAW_PATH} and {TABLE_PATH}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

#!/usr/bin/env python
"""Reproduce SVEAD claim C1 (AUC-ROC on cardio) and C2 (AUC-PR on cardio)."""
import os
import sys
import json
import time
import subprocess
import numpy as np

# Ensure local package is importable
sys.path.insert(0, os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))

from svead.data import load_cardio
from svead.metrics import evaluate_scores

RESULTS_DIR = "results"
RAW_PATH = os.path.join(RESULTS_DIR, "raw_cardio.json")
TABLE_PATH = os.path.join(RESULTS_DIR, "per_m_table.csv")
METRICS_PATH = os.path.join(RESULTS_DIR, "metrics.json")

# Target values from claim contract (for PASS/FAIL band only; not hard-coded into computation)
C1_TARGET = 0.9339
C2_TARGET = 0.5356
C1_TOLERANCE = 0.0189  # 3 * reported std 0.0063


def ensure_raw_results():
    if os.path.exists(RAW_PATH) and os.path.exists(TABLE_PATH):
        return
    print("Raw results missing; running experiments/run_cardio.py ...")
    subprocess.check_call([sys.executable, "experiments/run_cardio.py"], cwd=os.getcwd())


def main():
    os.makedirs(RESULTS_DIR, exist_ok=True)
    t0 = time.perf_counter()
    ensure_raw_results()

    with open(RAW_PATH, "r") as f:
        raw = json.load(f)

    records = raw["records"]
    provenance = raw["provenance"]
    config = raw["config"]

    # Build per-m summary
    m_grid = sorted(set(r["m"] for r in records))
    per_m = []
    for m in m_grid:
        rows = [r for r in records if r["m"] == m]
        aurocs = [r["auc_roc"] for r in rows]
        auprs = [r["auc_pr_primary"] for r in rows]
        times = [r["wall_time_s"] for r in rows]
        per_m.append({
            "m": m,
            "mean_auc_roc": float(np.mean(aurocs)),
            "std_auc_roc": float(np.std(aurocs, ddof=1)),
            "mean_auc_pr": float(np.mean(auprs)),
            "std_auc_pr": float(np.std(auprs, ddof=1)),
            "mean_wall_time_s": float(np.mean(times)),
            "n_seeds": len(rows),
        })

    # Select best m by mean AUC-ROC
    best = max(per_m, key=lambda x: x["mean_auc_roc"])
    best_m = best["m"]

    # Gather all repeats at best m
    best_rows = [r for r in records if r["m"] == best_m]
    best_aurocs = [r["auc_roc"] for r in best_rows]
    best_auprs = [r["auc_pr_primary"] for r in best_rows]

    c1_value = float(np.mean(best_aurocs))
    c1_std = float(np.std(best_aurocs, ddof=1)) if len(best_aurocs) > 1 else 0.0
    c2_value = float(np.mean(best_auprs))
    c2_std = float(np.std(best_auprs, ddof=1)) if len(best_auprs) > 1 else 0.0

    c1_verdict = "PASS" if abs(c1_value - C1_TARGET) <= C1_TOLERANCE else "FAIL"

    total_wall = time.perf_counter() - t0

    metrics = {
        "claim_C1": {
            "metric": "AUC-ROC",
            "value": round(c1_value, 6),
            "std_over_5_seeds": round(c1_std, 6),
            "dataset": "cardio",
            "split": "Unsupervised ADBench dataset; no train/test split stated in paper",
            "config": {
                "m_grid": config["m_grid"],
                "best_m": best_m,
                "ensemble_size_t": config["t"],
                "repeats": config["seeds"],
                "selection": "argmax mean AUC-ROC over m grid",
            },
            "target": C1_TARGET,
            "tolerance": C1_TOLERANCE,
            "verdict": c1_verdict,
            "notes": f"Reproduced {c1_value:.6f} ± {c1_std:.6f} at m={best_m}; paper reports {C1_TARGET}. "
                     f"Band ±{C1_TOLERANCE} corresponds to 3× reported std 0.0063.",
        },
        "claim_C2": {
            "metric": "AUC-PR",
            "value": round(c2_value, 6),
            "std_over_5_seeds": round(c2_std, 6),
            "dataset": "cardio",
            "split": "Unsupervised ADBench dataset; no train/test split stated in paper",
            "config": {
                "m_grid": config["m_grid"],
                "best_m": best_m,
                "ensemble_size_t": config["t"],
                "repeats": config["seeds"],
                "selection": "same run as C1",
            },
            "target": C2_TARGET,
            "notes": f"Reproduced {c2_value:.6f} ± {c2_std:.6f} at m={best_m}; paper reports {C2_TARGET}.",
        },
        "per_m_curve": per_m,
        "dataset_provenance": provenance,
        "timing": {
            "reproduce_py_wall_time_s": round(total_wall, 2),
            "estimated_compute": "CPU, ~1 min per run; 5 runs ~5 min per m",
        },
        "assumptions_applied": [
            "A2: StandardScaler fit on all rows, labels not used",
            "A3: best m selected by mean AUC-ROC over 5 seeds; fallback m=128 if search reduced",
            "A4: seeds [1,2,3,4,5]; RNG = numpy.default_rng(seed + 1000*m)",
            "A5: tie-break = lowest anchor index (numpy argmin)",
            "A6: dataset signature validated (1831x21, 176 anomalies, 0 NaN/inf)",
            "A7: all-NaN partition scores -> final 0",

            "C4": "Mean AUC-PR across 45 ADBench datasets — out of scope (CPU-only, budget)",
            "C5": "CPU runtime <3s for 500k instances — not measured (no synthetic 500k run)",
            "C6": "GPU runtime <1s for 500k instances — not reproducible (no GPU on this machine)",
        },
        "overall_verdict": "partially_reproduced",
    }

    with open(METRICS_PATH, "w") as f:
        json.dump(metrics, f, indent=2)

    print(f"C1 AUC-ROC = {c1_value:.6f} ± {c1_std:.6f} (target {C1_TARGET}, {c1_verdict})")
    print(f"C2 AUC-PR  = {c2_value:.6f} ± {c2_std:.6f} (target {C2_TARGET})")
    print(f"Best m = {best_m}")
    print(f"Total wall time: {total_wall:.2f}s")

import time
import numpy as np

sys.path.insert(0, os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))))

from svead.data import load_cardio
from svead.metrics import evaluate_scores

M = 2
T = 100
SEEDS = [1, 2, 3, 4, 5]
CHUNK_ROWS = 4096
RESULTS_DIR = "results"
OUT_PATH = os.path.join(RESULTS_DIR, "ablation.json")


def sample_anchors(n, m, rng):
    return rng.choice(n, size=m, replace=False)


def assign_cells(X, anchors, chunk_rows=4096):
    n, d = X.shape
    m = anchors.shape[0]
    cell_ids = np.empty(n, dtype=np.int64)
    distances = np.empty(n, dtype=np.float64)
    for start in range(0, n, chunk_rows):
        end = min(start + chunk_rows, n)
        block = X[start:end]
        x_norm = np.sum(block ** 2, axis=1, keepdims=True)
        a_norm = np.sum(anchors ** 2, axis=1, keepdims=True).T
        cross = block @ anchors.T
        dists_sq = x_norm + a_norm - 2.0 * cross
        dists_sq = np.maximum(dists_sq, 0.0)
        dists = np.sqrt(dists_sq)
        j = np.argmin(dists, axis=1)
        cell_ids[start:end] = j
        distances[start:end] = dists[np.arange(end - start), j]
    return cell_ids, distances


def cell_stats(X, anchors, cell_ids, distances):
    m = anchors.shape[0]
    delta_max = np.empty(m, dtype=np.float64)
    delta_mean = np.empty(m, dtype=np.float64)
    for j in range(m):
        mask = cell_ids == j
        if not np.any(mask):
            delta_max[j] = 0.0
            delta_mean[j] = 0.0
        else:
            cell_dists = distances[mask]
            delta_max[j] = cell_dists.max()
            delta_mean[j] = cell_dists.mean()
    return delta_max, delta_mean


def run_variant(X, variant, seed):
    """Run one variant at m=2, t=100.
    variant in {"dual", "ratio_only", "mean_only", "dual_drop_anchor"}
    """
    n, d = X.shape
    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed + 1000 * M)
    partition_scores = np.empty((T, n), dtype=np.float64)
    anchor_mask = np.empty((T, n), dtype=bool)  # True if point was anchor in partition

    for k in range(T):
        anchors = sample_anchors(n, M, rng)
        A = X[anchors]
        cell_ids, distances = assign_cells(X, A)
        delta_max, delta_mean = cell_stats(X, A, cell_ids, distances)
        point_delta_max = delta_max[cell_ids]
        point_delta_mean = delta_mean[cell_ids]
        cell_sizes = np.bincount(cell_ids, minlength=M)
        singleton = cell_sizes[cell_ids] == 1
        zero_max = point_delta_max == 0.0

        # Track anchor positions
        is_anchor = np.zeros(n, dtype=bool)
        is_anchor[anchors] = True
        anchor_mask[k] = is_anchor

        with np.errstate(divide="ignore", invalid="ignore"):
            ratio = np.where(zero_max, 0.0, distances / point_delta_max)
            mean_term = point_delta_mean

        if variant == "dual":
            scores = ratio * mean_term
        elif variant == "ratio_only":
            scores = ratio
        elif variant == "mean_only":
            scores = mean_term
        elif variant == "dual_drop_anchor":
            # Compute dual score, then mask out anchor positions for final mean
            scores = ratio * mean_term
            # Mark anchors as NaN so they are excluded from final nanmean
            scores = np.where(is_anchor, np.nan, scores)
        else:
            raise ValueError(variant)

        # Skip singleton cells (NaN)
        scores = np.where(singleton, np.nan, scores)
        partition_scores[k] = scores

    # Final aggregation
    if variant == "dual_drop_anchor":
        # nanmean ignores both singleton NaNs and anchor-masked NaNs
        with np.errstate(all="ignore"):
            final = np.nanmean(partition_scores, axis=0)
        final = np.where(np.isnan(final), 0.0, final)
    else:
        with np.errstate(all="ignore"):
            final = np.nanmean(partition_scores, axis=0)
        final = np.where(np.isnan(final), 0.0, final)

    return final


def main():
    os.makedirs(RESULTS_DIR, exist_ok=True)
    X, y, prov = load_cardio()
    print(f"Loaded cardio: X{X.shape}, anomalies={y.sum()}")

    variants = ["dual", "ratio_only", "mean_only", "dual_drop_anchor"]
    results = {}

    for var in variants:
        aurocs = []
        auprs = []
        times = []
        for seed in SEEDS:
            t0 = time.perf_counter()
            scores = run_variant(X, var, seed)
            dt = time.perf_counter() - t0
            m = evaluate_scores(scores, y)
            aurocs.append(m["auc_roc"])
            auprs.append(m["auc_pr_primary"])
            times.append(dt)
            print(f"{var} seed={seed}: AUC-ROC={m['auc_roc']:.4f} AUC-PR={m['auc_pr_primary']:.4f} time={dt:.2f}s")
        results[var] = {
            "auc_roc_mean": round(float(np.mean(aurocs)), 6),
            "auc_roc_std": round(float(np.std(aurocs, ddof=1)), 6),
            "auc_pr_mean": round(float(np.mean(auprs), 6)),
            "auc_pr_std": round(float(np.std(auprs, ddof=1)), 6),
            "mean_time_s": round(float(np.mean(times)), 4),
            "per_seed_auc_roc": [round(v, 6) for v in aurocs],
            "per_seed_auc_pr": [round(v, 6) for v in auprs],
        }

    out = {
        "best_m": M,
        "t": T,
        "seeds": SEEDS,
        "variants": results,
        "dataset_provenance": prov,
        "notes": (
            "Ablation at m=2 (best m from grid search). "
            "dual = δ/δmax·δmean (paper Eq. 2-3). "
            "ratio_only = δ/δmax alone. "
            "mean_only = δ/mean alone. "
            "dual_drop_anchor = dual score but zero-distance anchor partitions excluded from ensemble mean."
        ),
    }
    with open(OUT_PATH, "w") as f:
        json.dump(out, f, indent=2)
    print(f"Wrote {OUT_PATH}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

The main caveat is protocol, not fidelity: the grid search selects m by maximizing AUC-ROC on the same evaluation labels, and the optimum sits at the grid boundary m=2; m=4 (0.9249) is also inside the ±0.0189 band but every m≥8 fails the band (0.9075 at m=8), so the pass depends materially on the label-tuned hyperparameter choice that the paper describes but leaves underspecified. Full-data scoring with no train/test split matches the contract's stated split but is a disclosed high-risk assumption (A1/A9), since ADBench's standard unsupervised pipeline normally reports on a held-out test split. The run is not scaled down: the complete m-grid, t=100, 5 seeds and all 1831 cardio points were used; C3-C6 were simply not attempted and are disclosed as not reproduced. Minor provenance note: the ablation cited in the implementer summary was computed in an earlier run and was not regenerated by the final clean reproduce.py, so it cannot be re-verified from the final artifact.

requirement_check.evidence: svead_core.sample_anchors uses rng.choice(n, size=m, replace=False) — uniform sampling without replacement per partition.
assign_cells computes full Euclidean distances (chunked ||x||^2+||a||^2-2x·a) and takes argmin; no cell boundaries constructed.
score_partition: ratio = distances/point_delta_max, score = ratio * point_delta_mean, i.e. (δ/δmax)·δmean exactly as Eqs.(2)-(3).
cell_stats computes per-cell max and mean of anchor distances (anchor itself included with distance 0).
score_partition sets scores to NaN where cell size == 1; nanmean in svead_score aggregates only the partitions that scored the point (at m=2 the skipped fraction is 0).
Final score = np.nanmean over the t=100 partitions; A12 notes that at the selected m=2 no point is skipped, so this is identical to the plain arithmetic mean over t.
run_cardio.py explores m in {2,4,8,16,32,64,128,256} with t=100 fixed, and selects m by argmax mean AUC-ROC (best m=2).
Five seeds [1,2,3,4,5] per m; metric reported as mean ± std(ddof=1) in results/metrics.json and per_m_table.csv.
svead/metrics.py uses roc_auc_score and average_precision_score (plus a trapezoidal PR variant).

Labels are never used in scoring or in StandardScaler, but the grid-search selection of m maximizes AUC-ROC on the evaluation labels (assumption A3/A10, disclosed). The reported number is therefore the best of 8 label-selected hyperparameters, which mildly violates the strict 'labels only after predictions' reading.
Membership determined solely by nearest-anchor queries in assign_cells; no Voronoi boundaries/vertices computed.
Implementation is O(n·m·d·t) with a chunked distance kernel; structurally linear, though not empirically timed at 500k instances (that is C5's scope, explicitly not reproduced).
